comparison: Perfect agreement on metabolomics findings (C22-C25, C29). Both evaluations support the LC-MS/MS data showing β-alanine changes during infection. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these findings as part of the overall mechanism.
Complete agreement on host-derived β-alanine facilitating bacterial replication (C30-C33, C37). Both evaluations support the dose-dependent supplementation data and its implications for virulence.
Full agreement on control experiments (C34-C36) showing β-alanine effects are not mediated through altered macrophage immune responses (ROS/RNS, M1/M2 polarization).

Both support the exclusion of CycA as a β-alanine transporter (C39-C42). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of individual experiments; peer reviewers accepted these negative results as part of the overall transporter identification.
Both support the exclusion of GabP as a β-alanine transporter (C44-C45). OpenEval evaluates this separately; peer reviewers grouped it with other transporter findings.
Complete agreement on ArgT as the β-alanine transporter (C46-C47). Both evaluations support this finding, though OpenEval notes complementation experiments would strengthen the conclusion.
Full agreement on panD expression patterns (C50-C53). Both support the qRT-PCR and reporter data showing panD upregulation in intracellular conditions.

Strong agreement on panD's role in intracellular replication (C54-C58). Both evaluations support the gentamicin protection assays and complementation data. OpenEval provides detailed statistical assessment; peer reviewers found the work 'convincing.'

Both support the control experiments (C59-C60) showing no growth defect in rich medium. OpenEval evaluates this separately; peer reviewers accepted it as part of the intracellular replication findings.
Agreement on β-alanine rescue experiments (C61). Both evaluations support this critical demonstration that exogenous β-alanine complements the replication defect.
Perfect agreement on S. Typhi validation (C62-C63). Peer reviewers specifically praised these confirmatory experiments in human macrophages as providing evidence of relevance to human infections.

Complete agreement on the summary conclusion (C64) that bacterial-derived β-alanine is critical for intracellular replication. Both evaluations support this integration of multiple experimental lines.

Full agreement on in vivo virulence findings (C67-C79). Both evaluations support the dramatic mouse infection phenotypes. OpenEval provides detailed statistical assessment; peer reviewers found the multidisciplinary approach 'convincing.'
Complete agreement on RNA-seq findings (C80-C83). Both evaluations support the transcriptomic data and pathway analyses identifying metabolic changes in ΔpanD.
Full agreement on zinc transporter downregulation (C84, C87, C89-C92). Both evaluations support the RNA-seq and qRT-PCR validation showing β-alanine regulates znuABC expression.
Agreement on negative results (C94-C95) showing no effect on SPI genes. Both evaluations accept these findings as important for narrowing the mechanism to metabolic pathways.
Complete agreement on mechanistic interpretation (C96) that β-alanine affects virulence through metabolic regulation rather than SPI activation. Both support this conclusion from the RNA-seq data.
Full agreement on negative results (C97-C100) excluding other downregulated pathways as major contributors. Both evaluations accept these findings as narrowing focus to zinc transport.
Strong agreement on zinc transport as key pathway (C101-C103). Both evaluations support the mouse infection data identifying znuA as critical for the mechanism.
Agreement on zinc accumulation findings (C104-C105). Both evaluations support the data showing zinc accumulates in host cells when bacteria cannot take it up.
Complete agreement on epistasis analysis (C106-C109). Both evaluations support the double mutant experiments showing panD's virulence role is partially dependent on znuA.
Agreement on in vitro zinc accumulation (C110-C111). Both evaluations support this extension of in vivo findings to the macrophage system.
Agreement on in vitro epistasis (C112-C113). Both evaluations support the consistency between in vitro and in vivo epistasis analyses.
Agreement on rescue experiments (C114-C116). Both evaluations support the epistatic relationship demonstrated by zinc and β-alanine supplementation.
Agreement on summary conclusion (C117) linking β-alanine to zinc uptake. Both evaluations support this integration of multiple experimental approaches.

Strong agreement on the overall mechanism (C118-C119). Both evaluations support the model integrating host- and bacterial-derived β-alanine with zinc transporter regulation. Peer reviewers found the model 'adequately supported.'

Both evaluations rate this as UNCERTAIN (C120). OpenEval notes lack of quantitative evidence for 'large amount' claim; peer reviewers suggest further work needed on mechanistic details. Both appropriately recognize this as speculation.
Agreement on β-alanine regulation of zinc uptake as an additional mechanism (C126). Both evaluations support this novel finding while acknowledging prior knowledge of ZnuABC function.
Agreement on the integrated model (C127) linking β-alanine-mediated zinc uptake to known zinc functions in pathogenesis. Both evaluations support this synthesis of new and existing knowledge.

Agreement on therapeutic implications (C129-C130). Both evaluations support the potential relevance while appropriately recognizing this as speculation requiring further validation. Peer reviewers found the work 'valuable.'
